brief: brief-learned-capacity.md: JS-166's figures (a 3-core worker cannot help a 3.2-price 4K job, so the cluster holds one play and refuses a second; the 12-thread worker declares 3.5 under a CPU limit of 8, was throttled in 93% of periods and ran about 1.0x; operators cannot know a CPU's speed against the reference machine) and D-062's failed start-up benchmark. Owner's direction: a worker starts transcoding and recognizes when it is slowing down, so an operator declares no CPU.
tradeoff: Given up until JS-177 merges: an operator still declares a figure, and on a CPU slower than the reference or on SMT threads an undeclared worker overstates itself, so a play it cannot keep is admitted and stalls (BL-259). On the dogfood that means one 4K play at a time and a second refused as 'rate limits' until JS-166's sizing correction lands; viewers of an overstated worker wait for the first job's speed to be learned before the refusal with a reason is exact. No viewer or operator loses a capability.
entry: Option B: learning after JS-041, as JS-177 at priority 21, dependsOn JS-166 and JS-041, with BL-259's bars as criteria 2 to 4. A worker learns what it holds from the jobs it runs: price times measured speed, starting from its processors with a container CPU limit counted, lowered when jobs run under the 1.2x admission bound, raised slowly with margin and smoothed over minutes; transcodeCores becomes an optional ceiling, never required. The dogfood's sizing is corrected by configuration now, under JS-166: its declared figures from that task's job speeds, and the 12-thread worker's CPU requests equal to limits in whole cores (each a homelab change for the owner). The helper's full-price rule is intended for a play its worker holds alone; the dogfood's fault was the declared figure, and JS-177 criterion 5 handles it. BL-259 closes, promoted into JS-177. If JS-177 is too large for one build it splits into (a) criteria 2 to 4, 6 and 7 and (b) criterion 5, both ahead of JS-056. Rejected: A (a task now, ahead of the household set, delaying JS-041), C (guidance only, operators keep declaring), D (leave BL-259 to wait for its triggers). Reopens on: JS-166's replay staying under 1.0x outside the first 30 seconds for a cause a true capacity figure would have refused or shared (JS-177 then goes ahead of JS-041); the no_room slow-job reason counted while another worker had 0.78 of the price free; JS-177's design review finding that the figure cannot be told apart from a slow store.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Installing is boring'; 'Growing is adding machines'; 'Every component scales independently'; 'Nothing breaks the viewers' evening'. D-044: capacity is measured on the worker, not declared. Owner, 2026-11-23: a worker starts transcoding and recognizes when it is slowing down.
